text:
Alisha: quick proposal — consolidate per-route quota window units. right now we store `quota_window_ms` (bigint) in console.analytics.routes and the console UX converts it to human text. this causes a lot of weird edgecases and heavy cardinality in the analytics index when teams send non-standard values.

Alisha: propose adding `quota_window_seconds` (int) and a small `quota_window_label` enum (minute|hour|day|custom) then backfill and deprecate the ms field. goals: smaller index, canonical units, simpler UI.

Ben: sounds good. main concerns: backfill cost and reads during transition. queries use `quota_window_ms` in a few hot paths (billing p99). what's the plan to keep queries fast?

Carlos: +1 on label enum. my vote is dual-write at ingest for 14 days, read-adapter that prefers new col but falls back to ms. we can push an index on (tenant_id, route_id, quota_window_seconds) before cutover.

Dana: console changes: need to normalize existing saved filters and dashboards. some customers have dashboard widgets filtering on raw ms values. we should provide a migration map and expose a compatibility toggle in the rollout UX.

Ben: agree on dual-write, but can we avoid a full-table scan backfill? maybe incremental backfill by updated_at windows, and a fast path for routes with no custom windows (most customers).

Alisha: plan sketch: 1) add cols nullable; 2) dual-write at API edge + version flag; 3) build read adapter in query layer; 4) backfill in batches using updated_at, with fast path for default windows; 5) add index; 6) flip console to prefer new cols; 7) monitor regressions and rollback.

Carlos: migration SQL for step 1/2 (dev-friendly):
```sql
alter table console.analytics.routes add column quota_window_seconds int null;
alter table console.analytics.routes add column quota_window_label text null;
update console.analytics.routes set quota_window_seconds = (quota_window_ms / 1000)::int
  where quota_window_ms is not null and quota_window_ms % 1000 = 0;
-- leave odd-ms values for later manual reconciliation as `custom`
```

Carlos: we'll also add a small function to normalize on read: `get_quota_window_seconds(route)` that checks new col then falls back converting ms.

Dana: for dashboards: propose a migration job that maps ms filters to seconds equivalents and records mapping in `console.migration.audit` so we can surface any unmappable filters in the UI before flip. UX toggle labeled "Compatibility mode: quota windows (ms)".

Mike: infra note — when we create the new index, do it concurrently and watch write amplification. coordinate with pg replicas, and schedule during low-traffic window. I'll own the rollout window.

Ben: metrics to watch: console query p99, ingest path latency, index bloat, number of routes still on `custom` after each backfill run. add regression alert if p99 increases >10%.

Alisha: good call. also add an eval to Redwood Optimize to check cost-per-token telemetry for requests that hit the read adapter.

deploy-bot: deploy queued: feature/dual-write-quota-window -> canary env (sha: abc123).

Carlos: I'll implement read adapter + migration worker. targeting canary next week. posting detailed checklist in #eng-platform once done.

Alisha: thanks — please add an RFC doc link when you have it and tag me. small follow-up: what do we do about exports/archival (S3 snapshots) that currently store ms? need to include conversion in export pipeline.

Dana: noted — export pipeline change added to the checklist. will coordinate with data-exports.

Ben: I can help with the backfill job to ensure it retries idempotently and reports per-tenant progress.

Alisha: awesome. next: create a short runbook for rollback steps if the console flip causes issues.

Mike: will draft runbook and post it as PR to infra-runbooks.

Alisha: great. tagging owners: @Carlos (read adapter + migration worker), @Dana (console UX + dashboard mapping), @Mike (index + infra window), @Ben (backfill/resilience).
